title: The CSV is always summary-level, quotes comma-containing values, and downloads with the lower-case filename
custom_preconds: 1. At least one technician's Est. Lost Labor exceeds $1,000 (so a value contains a comma).
custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (CSV)" and check the filename.
2. Open the file in a plain-text editor and find the over-$1,000 value.
3. Check for any day rows in the file.
custom_expected:
1. The file downloads as "technician-utilization.csv" (lower-case as shipped, unlike the Title-Case PDFs).
2. The CSV shows the technician rows and the Summary row - always this summary-level content; it does NOT vary by the summary/expanded choice (no day rows).
3. Any value containing a comma (e.g. "$1,234.50") is wrapped in double quotes per standard CSV escaping, so the columns parse correctly.
